title: Septation of the Aortic Sac and Distal Outflow Tract of the Embryonic Heart, a Hitherto Neglected Factor in the Embryology of Variants and Malformations of the Aortic Arch Complex
content: The adult configuration of the aortic arch complex (AoAC) results from transformation of its embryonic precursor. Concepts of the embryology of variants and malformations of the AoAC traditionally focus on transformation processes that are driven by regression and persistence of embryonic vascular segments. However, such concepts cannot explain every variant or malformation since they neglect other morphogenetic processes involved in the transformation of the embryonic AoAC, such as blood vessel “migration”, and septation of the aortic sac (AoS) and distal outflow tract (OFT) of the embryonic heart. This article focuses on the hitherto neglected role of septation of the AoS and embryonic OFT in normal and abnormal patterning of the AoAC. It is shown (1) how phylogenetic “deviations” from the mammalian “standard” of AoS septation lead to the AoAC branching patterns found in non-mammalian vertebrates; and (2) how ontogenetic deviations from the human “standard” can lead to AoAC anomalies, such as “bovine arch”; subclavian artery as first branch of the aortic arch; anomalous origin of supra-aortic branches from the proximal ascending aorta; anomalous origin of one pulmonary artery from the proximal ascending aorta; anomalous origin of one common carotid artery from the proximal pulmonary trunk; and tritruncal hearts.
